latest_jta.summary: Nationalist students at Bratislava University continued a numerus clausus agitation against Jewish students, holding meetings, and the Young Men's Christian Association lent premises for an antisemitic numerus clausus meeting after the Rectorate refused use of university rooms. The article reports that disturbances took place that day.

The article reports that a text falsely presented as an Alliance Israelite Universelle proclamation calling for Jewish world domination was circulated in Geneva by Georges Oltramare, who publishes an antisemitic periodical. The Geneva Jewish community and the Alliance denounced the text as a forgery.

The article reports that Nazi students drove Jewish students out of the University Building in Vienna, pursued them along the Ringstrasse, and beat and injured them, also knocking down several old people in the street. Two named Zionist students were badly injured and a number of Jewish students sustained minor injuries.
The editor of the Yiddish daily Unser Express writes that a renewed boycott movement started by Polish antisemites has been launched against Jewish businesses in Poland.

The article reports that Jewish shopkeepers, especially in Christian quarters, are doing almost no business during the Christmas season because of a boycott campaign. It also reports that many Jewish shops in Vilna are closing after going bankrupt.

The Socialist press reports that policemen belonging to the Swastika Party broke up a meeting of Socialist policemen, shouting antisemitic slogans including "Jews' Slaves!" and "Perish Judea!". The Interior Minister and Police Presidium ordered an inquiry.

The Central Committee of the B'nai B'rith in Poland cables the American B'nai B'rith that antisemitic National Democratic students committed acts of violence against Jewish students, which spread from the universities to the streets. The article does not give dates or places.
The Organisation of Jewish Retail Shopkeepers in Warsaw heard reports on boycott picketing by National Democratic students outside Jewish shops and called on the authorities to stop it.

When Vilna University reopened, Christian students occupied all the seats on the right side of the lecture halls, leaving the left side to Jewish students. The Jewish students refused to sit and stood during the lectures in protest.

The Warsaw Jewish Community Administration states that excesses took place recently at Polish universities, where students tried to prevent Jewish students from attending lectures. The excesses spread to a number of towns.

A Latvian education official told the Seym Educational Commission that in many German secondary schools in Latvia, Jewish pupils are being insulted and beaten by fellow pupils influenced by the Nazi movement.

The article reports that National Democratic students attacked Jewish students at Vilna University, and that on a Tuesday morning the disturbances spread to the Faculty of Humanities, where several professors were beaten and Jewish students were hunted. Injuries occurred on both sides.

The article reports that Nazis in Grenadier Strasse in Berlin shouted "Perish Judea" and attacked Jews passing through the street from behind. A crowd of Jews then drove the Nazis off, and two of the Nazis were injured.

The article reports that the Gazeta Warszawska claimed the accused Jews would face court martial, and that police officers were dismissed after a disciplinary inquiry into charges of anti-Jewish behaviour during excesses in Vilna on November 10.

latest_research.summary: The Observatory on Antisemitism in Belgium reports that a paving stone was thrown through a third-floor window of the Orthodox Jewish community synagogue in Anderlecht, shattering the glass. The Observatory describes it as vandalism targeting a Jewish place of worship, and the US ambassador calls it an antisemitic attack. The perpetrator is unidentified.

Jewish News reports that a woman was filmed describing Jewish people as "killers and psychopaths" during a protest outside Sheffield Town Hall. South Yorkshire Police first recorded a hate incident. A later Jewish News report says police concluded the remarks did not amount to a recordable crime, and the lower, no-crime finding is the one noted here.

Two unknown persons threw Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel synagogue complex on Brunnenstraße in Berlin-Mitte in the early morning. According to reports the devices landed on the pavement and no one was hurt.

A 26-year-old Jewish student wearing a kippah was struck on the head with a folding spade outside the Hohe Weide synagogue, according to the sources. Police assumed an antisemitic motive, and a later court ruling is reported to have found a targeted attack on a Jew.

Unknown persons scratched swastikas into several gravestones at the Jewish cemetery on Krankenhausstraße in Cloppenburg, and state security police investigated for incitement to hatred. Police later reported that two teenagers admitted the act.
Witnesses told police that a group of about 15 people gathered in front of the synagogue, shouted and burned an Israeli flag. State security police took over the investigation.

Police reported that a 24-year-old Jewish man was assaulted on a tram in Erfurt after another man noticed his Star of David necklace. The attacker tried to drag him off the tram, kicked him and later threatened him, and is being investigated for a politically motivated hate crime.

Berlin police reported that an unidentified man punched a 60-year-old man to the ground in a park after learning that he was Jewish, and the victim had minor facial injuries. State security police are investigating suspected aggravated assault with an antisemitic motive.
Unknown persons damaged the glass of the synagogue entrance door with stones, and police found a partly burned Israeli flag in front of it, according to the reports. Three suspects were arrested.

About 180 people moved from the station forecourt toward the synagogue in an unregistered rally, and antisemitic chants were shouted, according to a press report. Church bodies described the events near the synagogue as antisemitic riots.

RIAS reports that a resident of an asylum shelter in Coburg attacked another resident with a knife because he took him for a Jew. The Coburg prosecutor's office is reported to have assumed the perpetrator was not criminally responsible.

The entrance door of a residential house in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg was sprayed with a Star of David. State security police investigated on suspicion of incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung), and the press reported that the marking apparently aimed to intimidate Jewish residents.
